audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit non-current marketable securities after purging their income
audit_findings.magnitude: $212.535 million, computed as $237.471 million of non-current securities less $24.936 million held in the rabbi trust; $2.42 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and current marketable securities but omits unrestricted non-current securities whose interest income was removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Securities classified as non-current assets have maturity dates greater than one year from the balance sheet date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the $413.342 million bridge equals April cash of $301.364 million plus current securities of $111.978 million. Adding the computed $212.535 million unrestricted balance would raise base value from $42.46 to about $44.88 per share, a 5.7% change. It would not close the gap to the $80.97 market price, but it materially changes stated intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the non-rabbi-trust securities are unrestricted and rerun every scenario with $212.535 million added to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Nuuly rental-product reinvestment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $232.411 million of FY2026 rental-product purchases; treatment in OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Rental-product amortization is charged through cost of sales, while purchases are recurring operating investment; adding back amortization without deducting maintenance purchases would overstate OE and its fitted trend.
audit_findings.evidence: Purchases of rental product were $ 232,411 , $ 175,697 , and $ 150,668 for fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes the recurring cash purchases and accounting treatment but does not establish how the supplied OE calculation treated them. FY2026 purchases equal 98.7% of the $235.5 million anchor, so even a partial omission could materially reduce value. This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated OE error.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each OE year from the cash-flow workpapers, separately identifying rental purchases, amortization, retirements and customer purchases; rerun the anchor and scenarios if purchases were not captured exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Future tax-credit capital contributions may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.863 million liability at April 30, 2026, comprising $14.707 million current and $12.156 million non-current; $0.31 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Contribution payments are financing outflows while the related tax benefits enter net income and OE; an unmatched liability would require a bridge deduction or consistent OE treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities for the present value of the estimated future capital contributions are recorded in "Accrued expenses and other current liabilities" and "Other non-current liabilities" in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated, but omission from the bridge is less than 0.8% of the $3.722 billion base equity value and only $0.31 per share. Moreover, the related filed investment asset was $27.854 million, $0.991 million greater than the liability, so deducting the liability without reconciling the asset would be incomplete. This scale cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $27.854 million investment asset, $26.863 million liability, remaining tax benefits and OE treatment; correct the bridge only for the resulting net amount.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 numerator retains an unusual $46 million donation
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.0 million pre-tax; a computed conservative dollar-for-dollar addback would increase the fitted anchor by about $7.4 million and base value by about $1.18 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The donation affects FY2026 earnings and therefore the final observation in the ten-year log-trend OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2026, the Company made a $46.0 million charitable contribution to a donor-advised fund, which is included in "Other expense" in our Consolidated Statements of Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The expense is demonstrated, while its recurring character and after-tax OE effect remain unresolved. Even treating the entire pre-tax amount as an OE addback—a conservative upper-bound sensitivity—would raise base value only from $42.46 to about $43.64 and buy-below from $29.72 to about $30.55, still far below the $80.97 price. If recurring, no addback is appropriate.
audit_findings.action: Verify the after-tax amount included in FY2026 OE and contribution history; document the classification, although it cannot change the present owner decision at the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 contains a nonrecurring tax-reserve release
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $22.008 million computed from the filed 4.4% uncertain-tax-position benefit applied to $500.172 million of pretax income; conditional log-trend effect about $4.4 million on the anchor and $0.71 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit left in FY2025 OE raises one observation used by the ten-year log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily due to the tax benefit from the release of a portion of our income tax reserves as a result of a lapse of the statute of limitations for federal tax purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve release is demonstrated, but inclusion in the supplied OE series is unresolved. If the full computed $22.008 million benefit were removed from FY2025 OE, the log-trend anchor would fall by about 1.9%, base value by about $0.71 per share and buy-below by about $0.50. That scale cannot change the conclusion relative to the $80.97 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the reserve release and associated interest-and-penalty benefit into FY2025 OE; normalize it if included and retain the sensitivity calculation in the audit record.

audit_findings.title: The post-year-end Nuuly facility purchase may mix earnings and bridge bases
audit_findings.magnitude: $59.597 million discounted lease liability and $92.989 million undiscounted payments extinguished; facility purchase price and recurring OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The April bridge reflects post-year-end cash and asset balances, while the historical numerator contains lease rent; future OE should substitute depreciation and maintenance investment without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: In March 2026, the Company purchased the Nuuly fulfillment center in Raymore, Missouri and terminated the corresponding lease which was set to expire in January 2039.
audit_findings.explanation: The April cash bridge already incorporates the acquisition-period cash position, and the filing demonstrates termination of the former lease. The record does not disclose the facility purchase price, facility-specific historical rent, depreciation or maintenance requirement, so the recurring numerator mismatch cannot be quantified or judged material. This is an unresolved basis-alignment issue, not a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the purchase closing statement and facility-level rent, depreciation and maintenance-capex schedule; confirm the April lease derecognition and rerun projected OE on a consistently owned-facility basis.
